ledger.claim: The three artifacts describe the same trip, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02819 and the trace runs from the recorded trip-start at 16:25:31 to trip-completion at 16:32:51. The trace is also unimpaired for policy purposes - 100.0% coverage, 45 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds - so no consequence under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) arises and the distance it measures stands as the measured distance for this trip.

On the governing trace figure of 3.96 km against the booked optimal of 3.2 km, the excess is 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of the optimal route and therefore above POL-RD-01's 20% percentage limb. POL-RD-01 requires this measurement to be taken from gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not from the rounded 4.0 km convenience copy on the trip record, and the rider cites the trace figure. I do not put the percentage limb forward as establishing the deviation on its own, because the clause requires both limbs to pass and the rider addresses the second limb squarely in a separate claim below.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'One-way streets'. That is an external traffic cause asserted with no evidence ID, and there is no traffic_advisory in this bundle: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code that fired is MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING). Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, which discards assertions that cite no evidence ID. I disclose the impairment of the artifact I rely on: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is cited for its absence alone, which POL-GEN-02(3) makes citable. The driver's account also has no artifact behind it at all - the chat log for this trip carries zero messages from either party.

No clause on this record supplies the driver with an amended optimal or with any reduction of the measured excess. The chat log carries zero messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction route is unavailable and its 200 m corroboration test cannot be run on the record; both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote and must not be given a substitute figure; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12's pooled-itinerary baseline does not apply and the 3.2 km booked optimal stands untouched.

The fare model on this trip is METERED and the trip record carries no quoted_fare_sgd, so POL-RD-11's bar on distance-and-time refunds for upfront-quoted trips does not apply here, and POL-RD-02's arithmetic is the operative remedy rather than the pass-through correction alone. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which records 1.0, as POL-RD-02 requires; the trip record does not carry that field at all and no higher multiplier may be assumed.

If the tribunal finds the deviation established, the POL-RD-02 computation is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 8.68, against a charged total of 9.64; the refund is 0.96, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the charged total, so the outcome would be PARTIAL_REFUND, rounded up to SGD 1.00. The rider asks for that figure only if establishment is found on the trace.

The rider's 60-day profile does not engage POL-RD-08's additional corroboration requirement. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, below the clause's trigger of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated, so the excess the rider has shown is to be decided on this trip's trace evidence and no corroboration beyond the trace may be demanded of this claim.

I concede the point the record will not carry. On the governing trace figure the excess is 0.76 km, which is not greater than 0.8 km, and POL-RD-01 requires both the percentage and the absolute limb to pass; the rider therefore does not ask the tribunal to find the deviation established and does not ask it to read the threshold any other way. The two distance fields on this record straddle that threshold by 40 metres - 0.76 km on the trace, 0.80 km on the rounded copy - and the policy resolves the straddle against the rider by making the trace figure govern, so the shortfall is the rider's and the rider says so.

The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the trip record, and on the trace no deviation is established. EV-GPS-02819 records trace_distance_km of 3.96 km; EV-TRIP-02819 stores the booked optimal_distance_km as 3.2 km. The excess is therefore 0.76 km, which the platform's own derived block states as excess_km 0.76 / excess_pct 23.75 and tags status 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 is a two-limb gate: a deviation is ESTABLISHED only when the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. The percentage limb is cleared at 23.75%, but the absolute limb fails by 0.04 km. No deviation exists, and under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The threshold test fails even on the reading most favourable to the rider. POL-RD-01 fixes which field governs where the two distance fields disagree: gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs, and trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy that may NOT be cited for the threshold test. EV-TRIP-02819 rounds the same measurement up to 4.0 km, and 4.0 km less the 3.2 km optimal is exactly 0.80 km — not greater than 0.80 km. The absolute limb therefore fails on the rounded figure as well, so the result is the same whichever field is read.

The 3.2 km comparator is not displaced by any adjustment clause, so the threshold arithmetic above stands as measured. EV-TRIP-02819 carries pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at as null and amended_optimal_distance_km as null, so there is no re-quote and POL-RD-05 cannot run; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and solo_optimal_distance_km is not in issue. The booked optimal of 3.2 km is the correct baseline for POL-RD-01.

The trace is unimpaired, so the measured figure can be relied on and no gap-handling consequences arise. EV-GPS-02819 carries 45 fixes at a 10 second sample interval against a 10 second expected interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 — a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 seconds — is met, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not engaged. The deviation finding, such as it is, rests on a clean trace.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The rider must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. No artifact in this bundle shows an excess above 0.8 km; the highest figure available anywhere is the 0.76 km on EV-GPS-02819, and the rounded copy on EV-TRIP-02819 yields at most 0.80 km, which does not exceed the threshold. The burden never shifts to the driver, and there is nothing for the driver to excuse.

For completeness on the driver's side, the asserted traffic cause does not exonerate anything, and I do not ask the tribunal to treat it as if it did. The driver's statement is 'One-way streets'. The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this corridor: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own note records that no advisory covers the Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres corridor in this window. That impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run — there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses and no validity window to compare — and under POL-RD-13 the uncited traffic assertion carries no weight and neither reduces nor supplies an amended optimal. That costs the driver nothing, because the excess never reaches the POL-RD-01 threshold in the first place.

The absent advisory does not turn this into an escalation. Under POL-RD-13(1), where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The driver's statement cites no advisory identifier, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire on account of the traffic explanation.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the deviation gate fails and the fare already charged stands. The governing distance is the GPS trace, EV-GPS-02819, which measures 3.96 km; the booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-02819 is 3.2 km. The excess is therefore 0.76 km, or 23.75% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The percentage limb passes (23.75% > 20%), but the absolute limb fails (0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km). The trace figure governs and the trip record's rounded 4.0 km may not be used for the threshold test; even that figure gives exactly 0.80 km, which likewise is not greater than 0.80 km. No deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs the outcome NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The SGD 9.64 charged on EV-FARE-02819 stands and the SGD 1.50 the rider contests is not returned. This is not a win for either side on the merits of the route; it is the threshold doing its job.

No adjustment clause displaces the 3.2 km baseline. The trip record carries no amendment (pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), so POL-RD-05 cannot run. The vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The chat log EV-CHAT-02819 carries zero messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction route is unavailable and its 200 m test cannot be run.

The driver's explanation 'One-way streets' is an external-traffic assertion with no traffic_advisory behind it. EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 that assertion carries no weight and exonerates nothing. It does not need to: the excess never reaches the threshold, so nothing turns on it, and no escalation follows from the missing advisory because no party cited the absent identifier.

Nothing else is refundable. EV-FARE-02819 shows ERP of 0.00 with no gantries, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, so there is no billing-integrity defect and no POL-RD-09(4) referral. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (45 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. All three deciding artifacts carry trip TRP-02819 with consistent timestamps, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) are excluded. The driver profile, EV-DPROF-02819, shows 1 deviation flag in 90 days against 314 completed trips — far below the POL-RD-06 pattern test — so there is no conduct referral and no FULL_REFUND uplift. The rider's own POL-RD-02 arithmetic (recomputed fare 8.68 against a charged total of 9.64, a refund of 0.96 rounded up to SGD 1.00) is not reached, because that computation only runs once a deviation is established. Confidence is 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-GPS-02819 and EV-TRIP-02819) that carry the deciding measurement. The monetary effect is nil, below the automatic execution threshold, so no amount moves.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
